sealed.rule: DO NOT REGENERATE. The package root is bound to PASS_C2_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION at that commit. Post-PASS work that edits a formerly bound source, such as c2_corrective_run_update_v3.py gaining the successor and gated_historical modes, is tracked by commit history and lives on a branch after the sealed commit. Rebuilding the manifest over the changed tree would produce a different root and silently break the external binding. If a future package generation is genuinely required, it must be a NEW package with its own identity, and the packager must first be repaired to read committed bytes read-only per the recorded tooling follow-up.

review_repairs_applied.index_mode_fail_open: authority_path_dirty compared only the index object id, so a staged --chmod flip preserved the blob and evaded the authority gate whenever the path was a declared modification. The bound mode is now passed in and compared.
review_repairs_applied.loader_member_toctou: The loader authenticated each member by path and then reopened the metadata and registry to parse them. A same-length metadata forgery injected in that interval was returned with membership_donor_set_sha256 of all zeros while both external roots still reported correct. Members are now read once into memory; lengths, digests and both roots are computed from those captured bytes and parsing happens from the same buffers, so no member is reopened after authentication. Symlinks, reparse points, subdirectories and unmanifested extras are refused. The regression asserts the metadata is opened exactly once, because a second open is the attack surface.

review_repairs_applied.toctou: The source was hashed by path and then reopened, so the recorded digest could describe one revision while availability was derived from another, and source_bytes came from a still later stat. review_repairs_applied.toctou_regression_strength: The first TOCTOU test contained an `assert ... or True`, which proves nothing, and never ran the full builder while the backing file changed. review_repairs_applied.writer_byte_binding: Found by the peer, not by me: the writer wrote each member and then reopened the path to hash it, so a same-length substitution in that interval became the bytes the manifest recorded while the builder still returned the original in-memory metadata. The manifest is now derived from the exact in-memory payloads before anything is written, so a write-time substitution makes the directory fail verification instead of redefining the authority. This was the writer-side twin of the reader-side interval I had already closed, and I had not looked for it.

promotion_successor.blocking_design_finding: V20 cannot be promoted by flipping a flag. Its verifiers raise unless real_execution_ready is not False, so they accept only False, while its production entrypoints raise unless it is not True, so they proceed only on True. The two are mutually exclusive by construction, which is what makes V20 permanently unready. A promotion successor therefore needs its own authority schema, verifier and entrypoint triple wrapping accepted V20, and may not reuse V20's verifier.

self_audit_20260908.finding_1: authority_path_dirty measured dirtiness with `git status` against current HEAD rather than the checkpoint-bound commit. After a later commit replaced a declared authority the worktree was clean against the new HEAD, so a completely different file could stand in for the authority with no authority-level complaint. Worse, a test had ratified this as expected behaviour. Dirtiness is now the comparison of the bound tree entry object id against `git hash-object --path`, which applies the same clean filter a commit would, so it is exact on a CRLF checkout with no line-ending handling in Python and touches neither the index nor the object store.
self_audit_20260908.finding_2: The availability builder admitted an existing empty output directory and then called mkdir(exist_ok=False), dying with an unhandled FileExistsError instead of working or stopping cleanly.
self_audit_20260908.finding_3: While repairing finding 1 a file rewrite truncated seven authority-identity attack tests. Detected by the suite count falling from 30 to 24 rather than by reading the diff; restored from HEAD and reconciled to 31 passing cases.
self_audit_20260908.finding_4_external: Independent review then found the TOCTOU and index-protection defects above, plus four lower-level authority/governance defects. tooling_followups.C2_PACKAGER_GIT_BYTES_READ_ONLY: git_bytes() currently runs 'git add -- <path>' then 'git show :<path>'.
